text:
The Rangers arrive in Seattle with two straight wins after a 1-3-0 slide, outscored 20-14 over their last five and still without defenseman Sean Durzi and goalie Igor Shesterkin. Braden Schneider has moved in beside Pettersson and is up to 20:22 a night from 18:11. The Kraken are 3-2-0 in their last five after Matty Beniers won it in overtime against Calgary, and they're missing Jared McCann, with Jordan Eberle now beside Beniers and Mackie Samoskevich. Tye Kartye and Eeli Tolvanen, both former Kraken, return to Seattle for the first time.

New York has controlled more of the play at five on five (52% of the expected goals, which measure chance quality, against 45% for Seattle). Our model projects 3.26 goals for the Rangers tonight and 2.9 for Seattle. On special teams, the Rangers' power play creates 0.66 expected goals a game to Seattle's 0.58. Seattle's projected starter, Joey Daccord, has a .889 save percentage this season and is 1.43 goals worse than expected, after finishing 6.1 below expected last year. New York's goalie is not yet known.

Alexis Lafrenière, the first overall pick in 2020, is at 31% to score. Berkly Catton carries a seven-game point streak for the Kraken, and as Sound of Hockey asks, "Is Berkly Catton the star the Kraken have been waiting for?" Our under-the-radar pick is Pavel Dorofeyev: 4.8 expected goals over his last 10 games, better than 99% of depth forwards, and we have him at 32% to score.
